author: fradamt
content:
Just wanted to check if people have opinions on the idea of limiting PQ registration to 0x02 validators, as a forcing function for migration from 0x01 and hopefully consolidation. The process would then be:
1. Migrate a validator to 0x02
2. Register a PQ key for it
3. Optionally, consolidate other 0x01 validators into it

If that's what it takes to make this viable, we could add the custom sweep threshold functionality.  Could be the difference between having to handle 500k validators or 50-100k (right now we have 25k 0x02 validators, representing 45% of the stake). It's a huge difference! With 100k we could maybe even consider not having aggregators at all, just a single global topic, and then the proposer aggregates once (no recursion)?

author: barnabemonnot
content:
Agree on using the PQ transition as a forcing function but also need to make sure that there aren't "very good reasons" for 0x01 vals to move to 0x02.

Less sure about ability to make design decisions on aggregation topology based on the effective number of validators, without an active cap. We always need to plan for the worst-case sadly. I'd be very much in favour of introducing a very generous cap such as 500k or 250k, so that we at least fix that variable somewhere. My intuition is that it would even lower MinEB, given the pace of consolidations. Just seems like a win win all around.

author: alexey_91090
content:
Hi all! I was experimenting with streaming strategies of XMSS aggregation and found some interesting results

First of all how to read graphic: first part is distribution of bls attestations from real Fulu slot from 4/64 subnets to match what we plan to have from 1/16 subnets (with XMSS network propagation will be different, but it is good datapoint to start). This is epoch boundary slot, so it is closer to worst case scenario which we should handle. I measured for different slot deadlines 4s/6s/8s/10s from slot start for upstream main. Metric that is important for real situation is coverage (amount of votes we aggreagted / amount of votes we received from network before deadline) it is used instead of total votes bc we should have better network protocols to make propagation faster

Strategy that I compare is waiting all votes and merge at once or use greedy batching like we usually do in bls approach. Last batch was triggered on some statistics from prev runs on how fast we process votes, so it can work better with other strategies. And with greeady here we have much better results

With that the votes we actually miss because of performance are only that we received during last batch. With that performance is important when we have tight deadlines/faster network/distribution shifted closer to deadline. Otherwise big 1400 batch optimisation doesn't give a lot benefits

Numbers are from box with next CPU: AMD EPYC 4585PX (Zen 5) 16 physical cores and RAM: 64 GB DDR5-5600, 2 × 32 GB. Build with enabling of only AVX2 instructions and was running on 4/8 cores setup

author: ethdreamer
content:
claude's answer:

  **leanvm-sidecar vs lean-pq bindings: are they compatible?**
  From reading git history and source in both repos. Nothing was built or run.

  **Aggregation proofs: not compatible today**
  - `lean-pq` 0.10.1 pins leanVM `5e3ade21` (Nov 8). Its main branch and pending 0.11.0 release are on the same pin.
  - The sidecar first exists at leanVM `11f3732e` (Nov 18).
  - In between, leanVM changed its challenge field from 192 to 128 bits (`cad2da9f`, Nov 13), plus the guest program. Proofs from before that can't be verified after it.
  - All the breaking changes landed before the sidecar was added, so no leanVM commit has the sidecar and still verifies `lean-pq` 0.10.1 proofs.
  - leanVM `main` is probably already incompatible with the sidecar's first commit, and open PRs change the prover further.

  **Raw signatures: compatible**
  - leanXMSS scheme and encoding (32-byte pubkey, 2404-byte signature) are unchanged from `5e3ade21` to today; known-answer test files match.
  - So a client can sign and verify individual signatures with `lean-pq` 0.10.1 and do all aggregation and proof verification through the sidecar.

  **Revision drift is silent**
  - The sidecar handshake's verifier tag (`leanvm-v1`) was not bumped for the field change.
  - Nodes on different revisions will connect fine, then fail to verify each other's proofs with no version error.
  - leanVM's existing release tags all predate the sidecar.

  **Proposed asks**
  1. All clients build the sidecar from one exact leanVM commit.
  2. leanVM team: cut a tag for the devnet, and bump the verifier tag on breaking changes.
  3. `lean-pq` maintainers (if anyone wants the in-process route): re-pin to that same commit and expose proof bytes and claims bytes separately.

author: .paulharris
content:
i really think we should be careful conflating things we want with things we need. We do *need* no 0x00 validators, but the idea of pulling in custom ceilings in order to have PQ data registration for 0x02 is pretty weird, and in real terms all we're looking at is reducing the active count of validators.
IMO saying 'consolidations are disappearing, so use it or lose it' would drive the behaviour at least as much, without pulling in custom ceilings
